purpose: Ownership and regeneration provenance for the generated artifacts under the governed roots. Each entry records which existing Makefile command regenerates a file (or class of files) and whether the file may be hand-edited. This registry records ownership and regeneration provenance only; it does not certify statistical validity, methodology, or predictive value, and asserts no investment merit. The no-reliable-predictive-edge conclusion and the research-support-only boundary are unchanged.
curation: Hand-curated and reviewed input, like model_confidence_contract.json. NOT a generated file. Every generator_command below cites an existing Makefile target confirmed against the writer in scripts/ or experiments/ (writers were read, not inferred from filenames). Regenerate artifacts only through their owning command; never hand-edit a generated file.
coverage_rule: Every file under a governed root, excluding experiments/results/runs/**, must be matched by exactly one entry below. An unmatched file (orphan) or a file matched by more than one entry (duplicate ownership) is a governance failure enforced by tests/test_artifact_registry.py.
prospective_entry_rule: prospective_entries[] carries the frozen ownership contract for governed outputs whose registration requires ownership to be fixed before the run that creates them (docs/thesis/STAGE_1B_REGISTRATION.md, 'Governance wiring required before the first Stage 1b execution'; docs/thesis/STAGE_2_REGISTRATION.md, 'Implementation-time governance wiring — 2026-09-03'). Each item has the same shape as an entries[] item and the same 'make <target>' generator_command rule, but is not yet subject to coverage_rule because its files do not exist yet and every entries[] entry must match at least one real file. When the governed run creates the files, that run's commit moves these items verbatim into entries[] and removes them from here; nothing about an item may change during that move.

coverage_exclusions.reason: Per-run manifest directories accumulate one directory per 'make research' run. They are governed as a class by the run_manifest entry below and by METHODOLOGY 'Run-directory governance', not enumerated per file.

artifact_class_definitions.generated: Deterministic output of a Makefile-invoked generator. Regenerate via generator_command; never hand-edit.
artifact_class_definitions.run_manifest: Per-run provenance manifest written by 'make research'. Generated provenance; immutable once written (see METHODOLOGY run-directory governance).
artifact_class_definitions.human_document: Hand-authored / human-reviewed document. Owned by a human editor, not a generator; hand_edit_forbidden is false.
artifact_class_definitions.source_input: Manually curated raw input. Lives under data/trusted_raw/, outside these governed roots; listed here only for vocabulary completeness.
artifact_class_definitions.runtime_output: Output produced by the running application at request time. Outside these governed roots; listed here only for vocabulary completeness.
artifact_class_definitions.proposed_future: Artifact named by a future task but not yet created. Intentionally has NO entries[] entry until the file exists, because every entries[] entry must match at least one real file. Where a registration fixes ownership BEFORE the run that creates the file, the frozen ownership contract is declared in prospective_entries[] instead, and the run commit moves it verbatim into entries[].

checksum_verification.rule: Reports that embed a top-level source_artifacts list of {path, sha256} objects are re-verified: each referenced path is re-hashed and compared to the recorded sha256. A mismatch is stale evidence — regenerate the report via its generator_command or investigate the upstream change. The sole current-state exception is the exact historical experiments/significance.py hash transition registered in tests/test_artifact_registry.py for the frozen excess-basis and serving-eval reports; those historical artifact bytes and recorded hashes remain untouched. The verification set is auto-discovered across the governed roots by the test, so newly added reports are covered automatically.

reproducibility_note: Regeneration reproduces content in an environment-qualified sense only: byte identity requires matching Python, platform, and numerical-package versions (see METHODOLOGY 'Reproducibility and run provenance'). This registry does not claim universal byte reproducibility.
